Thanks for the review. All points addressed:

1. **Silent breaker trip** — the logError message now explicitly states that undo/restore will be unavailable. The existing logWarning on skip already surfaces in logs.
2. **patch()/diff() ignoring add() failure** — both now check the add() result and bail out early if it returns false, avoiding git diff against a stale index.
3. **Init failures not feeding the breaker** — init now checks the result code and calls recordFailure on failure, so persistent init errors can trip the breaker.
4. **Missing Windows OOM patterns** — added 'not enough storage is available', 'not enough memory resources', and 'insufficient memory' to transientPatterns. Tests added.
5. **Test coverage** — added test cases for all new Windows OOM patterns in transient-error.test.ts.
6. **Hardcoded constants** — retryDelay and circuitThreshold are now configurable via SNAPSHOT_RETRY_DELAY_MS and SNAPSHOT_CIRCUIT_THRESHOLD env vars.

Added circuit breaker tests covering the previously untested logic:

Ran the same probe from a different angle — raw HTTP against `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` (non-stream, 2026-09-14, headers `User-Agent: opencode/x`, `Accept-Encoding: identity`, `x-opencode-session` constant). Independent confirmation of the glm-5.3-flash behavior, plus two additions:

**1. Byte-identical re-request test** (stronger than consecutive-turn observation): same messages, re-sent byte-for-byte after 10s:

| model | request with replayed `reasoning_content` | byte-identical re-request (+10s) |
|---|---|---|
| `glm-5.3` | cached 640/736 | **640/736 = 87%** |
| `glm-5.3-flash` | 0/717 | **0/717 = 0%** |
| `omen-alpha` | 0/734 | 0/734 |

A byte-identical re-request is the easiest possible cache hit; glm-5.3-flash never engages, so this looks route-level rather than cache-affinity or timing.

**2. On glm-5.3 the hit extends through the replayed reasoning_content.** Its second request hit 640 tokens while the first request's *input* was only 195 tokens — the cached prefix matched the prior request's generation-side sequence (input + reasoning + content), i.e. that route preserves thinking by default and the cache covers the replayed CoT. This matches Z.ai's official Preserved-Thinking cache design (docs.z.ai → Thinking Mode → Preserved thinking, "increases cache hit rates").

**3. The GLM `thinking` object is rejected with 400 on every GLM route** (`{"thinking":{"type":"enabled","clear_thinking":false}}` → `invalid request body: json: unknown field "thinking"`, error cites the Console Go upstream). That flag enables Preserved Thinking — default-on on GLM's own Coding Plan endpoint and listed in glm-5.3-flash's official recommended parameters — so it is currently impossible to opt in via OpenCode Go. May be worth checking whether the flash/omen routes cache correctly with preserved thinking enabled upstream, or whether caching simply isn't wired on those routes.

Also observed: `prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` is always `null` on these routes.

Related: #48116 (same byte-identical method; deepseek-v4-flash / qwen3.8-max also never cache, glm-5.2 does), #43218. Happy to re-run against any route.

**Distinct trigger, same crash: an agent that used to exist was removed from config**

Environment: opencode `1.18.30` (the build bundled with OpenChamber 1.23.1), macOS, `POST /session/{sessionID}/prompt_async`.

Unlike the plugin-defined case here and the `name`-field case in #42507, this agent was a normal config-defined primary agent (`agent/Beratung.md`) that had worked for weeks. It was then removed from config. Existing sessions still carry that name in `session.agent`, so **every** subsequent prompt dies with `Die(UnknownError)` — the sessions become permanently unusable, and there is no UI recovery path: the agent is no longer selectable, while the stored name keeps being sent.

Repro:
1. Define a primary agent (here `Beratung`); run sessions with it.
2. Delete its definition from config.
3. `GET /agent` no longer lists it; send `POST /session/{id}/prompt_async` with `{"agent":"Beratung","noReply":true,"parts":[{"type":"text","text":"ping"}]}`.
4. HTTP 204, then no message/part is written and the log shows:

```
level=ERROR message="prompt_async failed" sessionID=ses_… cause="Cause([Die(UnknownError: UnknownError)])"
```

5. Re-adding the identical definition makes the same request succeed (204, message stored). A/B confirmed on the same session.

Two things make this undiagnosable (relevant to every issue in this cluster):
- `NamedError.create` calls `super(name)`, so `.message === "UnknownError"`; the real text (`Agent not found: "Beratung". Available agents: …`) exists only in `.data.message` and is dropped by every path that prints or forwards the error. That is why the UI shows only `UnknownError: UnknownError`.
- For this path the `session.error` event is not persisted either (0 error events in the session's aggregate), so subscribers receive nothing.

Ask: fall back to the session's configured agent and from there to the default agent — the CLI already does this ("agent not found. Falling back to default agent"), while the HTTP/session path instead dies. At minimum, surface `.data.message`.

Correcting my own report: this is a duplicate, and my framing was wrong.

The 429 `FreeUsageLimitError` evidence I included was a **red herring** — that response came from my own `curl` calls to the Zen endpoint, not from opencode. The crash happens **client-side in `SystemPrompt.environment`, before any provider request is made**, which is precisely why no provider error appears in the log. There is no provider error being masked; my "error-surfacing" angle was based on a false causal link.

The root cause is the 1.18.30 regression tracked in #48645 (regression window narrowed to 1.18.29 → 1.18.30), and in #48903, #48372, #48811.

The "ruled out" section of my report still stands and is consistent with a version regression: empty config, MCP removed, plugin removed (config *and* cached package), skills moved aside, fresh state directory, different models, and a clean `brew reinstall` of 1.18.30 all fail identically — because none of them touch the actual bug.

Fixes reported in #48645: downgrade (1.18.29 verified good by A/B comparison; `npm install -g opencode-ai@1.18.15` also reported working), or reinstall from `anomalyco/tap`.

Happy for this to be closed as a duplicate.

+1 I hit this daily in my real workflow.

Use case: monorepo with multiple apps, each in its own manually created worktree (wt-vela, wt-canalis, wt-mdl, etc.), each on a different branch, running in parallel.

Issues I see in Desktop (v1.18.29):

Manual worktrees are invisible, git worktree add creates wt-* directories, but Desktop doesn't detect them at all. I have to cd into each worktree and run opencode from CLI every time.
Opening multiple worktrees replaces the existing project, all worktrees share the same git common-dir, so Desktop keys project ID by root commit hash. Opening wt-canalis silently replaces the wt-vela session I already had open (same root cause as #5638).
No branch switcher in the UI, there's no way to switch branches without closing the session and reopening from CLI.
What I'd like:

Desktop should detect existing worktrees for the same repo (read the .git file in each worktree to find commondir)
Show all worktrees as tabs within a single workspace, not as separate projects
Add a compact branch indicator in the UI (worktree name + branch name)

Reproduced on the **release channel**, `opencode v2.0.3` (macOS 26 / Darwin 27, arm64, bun global install) — so this has shipped to stable, not just next/beta.

**Root cause confirmed in code** (v2 branch):

- `packages/cli/src/server-process.ts:149` — the spawned `serve --service` correctly detects `EADDRINUSE` and produces the actionable message, including the `service set port` hint.
- `packages/client/src/effect/service.ts:122` — a finished contender's failure is returned only when `contenders.size === 0`. Because the ensure loop keeps one candidate plus one lock probe in flight, each failure arrives while another contender is still pending, so the specific error is dropped every iteration; line 138 then throws the generic `Timed out waiting for the background service to start` with no `cause`. Same pattern in `packages/client/src/promise/service.ts:59`.
- Suggested fix: retain the most recent contender failure and attach it as `cause` to the final timeout error.

**One extra data point on how the port gets poisoned with no visible listener:** in my case `lsof -nP -iTCP:49374 -sTCP:LISTEN` showed *nothing*, and a manual Python `bind()` with `SO_REUSEADDR` still failed with `EADDRINUSE`. The culprit was a stale **ESTABLISHED** loopback connection, `127.0.0.1:49383 -> 127.0.0.1:49374`, held by the Tailscale GUI app (no `tailscale serve`/`funnel` config — a coincidental ephemeral-range collision; the hidden peer end was likely a root-owned process, invisible to user-level `lsof`). On Darwin, `SO_REUSEADDR` only permits rebinding when prior sockets are in `TIME_WAIT`; an *active* socket with that local port blocks `bind()` regardless. Quitting Tailscale closed the connection and the managed service started immediately and healthily.

So "nothing is listening on the port" does **not** rule out this failure mode — `lsof -nP -iTCP:<port>` *without* the LISTEN filter (or `netstat -an`) is needed, which makes the missing error message even more costly.

I proxied every request. The first one is normal: roles=[system, user]. After it returns, opencode sends the next one as roles=[system, user, assistant], with no new user message and the assistant's own reply sitting last. The root turn spawned a `task` (explore, `mode=subagent`) child; the child raised six `external_directory` asks (`action=ask` in the log) and the client never received a `session/request_permission` frame for them — `acp/permission.ts` `process()` does `tryGet(permission.sessionID)` and returns when the child session is not in the ACP session store (`acp/session.ts` only stores sessions from `session/new`/`load`/`resume`/`fork`). Seem like a no-brainer to have a provider which can consume LiteLLM’s `/model/info` metadata to get limits, costs, modalities, and capabilities. It seemed like [PR 8359](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/8359) addresses this and got stalled so I investigated:

### What Happened
1. PR #8359 (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/8359) initially implemented GET {baseURL}/models for @ai-sdk/openai-compatible providers.
2. During review, several design questions appeared:
- Should discovery be automatic or opt-in?
- Should the endpoint merely add models, or filter Models.dev to the models the account can access?
- How should authenticated endpoints be queried?
- How long may discovery delay startup?
- What happens when /models provides only an ID and no limits or capabilities?
3. The implementation caused an E2E problem because OpenCode’s own endpoint exposed additional models. A test selected an unexpected model and was denied. The immediate workaround was to skip discovery for the opencode provider.
4. On January 30, 2026, maintainer rekram1-node merged it into models-endpoint, not dev, saying:
“Merging into a separate branch that I'll play with for a bit and see if tweaks are needed”
5. That branch then received two commits named wip. One changed discovery toward filtering known models and left adding unknown endpoint models unfinished.
6. PR #13234 (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/13234) was opened to merge models-endpoint into dev. It received no maintainer review and became increasingly stale.
7. On May 15, PR #13234 was automatically closed because it was older than one month and had fewer than two positive reactions.

### Why It Stalled
The fundamental issue was that /v1/models discovery solves only part of the problem.
The standard response usually provides:
```
{
  "id": "model-name",
  "object": "model",
  "owned_by": "..."
}
```
That does not provide the information OpenCode relies on for:
- Context and output limits
- Costs
- Vision and PDF support
- Reasoning capabilities
- Tool support
- Temperature support
- Provider-specific transport behavior

That deficiency was explicitly raised on both #8359 and #13234. It is exactly why generic discovery would not have removed your need for the /.well-known/ metadata.

Other unresolved concerns were:
- Whether inaccessible Models.dev models should be hidden
- Whether configured models should survive if discovery fails
- Authentication availability during config/provider initialization
- Startup delays from unreachable endpoints
- Automatic outbound requests to arbitrary custom URLs
- Unknown models receiving context: 0, output: 0, and conservative capability default

Correcting my own earlier scope comment on this issue. I re-checked it against the current code and all three gaps I listed are already implemented there, so please treat my plan as withdrawn rather than pending. Details, with the code I read:

**1. The wait time is already surfaced, and it ticks.** The card you quoted (`повтор через 3 с - попытка №2`) is the retry countdown:

- `packages/session-ui/src/components/session-retry.tsx:14-27` recomputes `seconds = (status.next - Date.now()) / 1000` on a 1 s interval;
- `packages/session-ui/src/timeline/session-timeline-row.tsx:534-546` builds that status from the assistant message as `{ type: "retry", attempt: retry.attempt, message: retry.error.message, next: retry.at }`, and the row is inserted by `packages/session-ui/src/timeline/projection.ts:270` and rendered in the app through `packages/app/src/session/timeline/message-timeline.tsx:22-23`;
- your exact wording is these i18n keys: `ui.sessionTurn.retry.retrying` / `inSeconds` / `attemptLine` (`packages/ui/src/i18n/ru.ts:67-70`).

So `retry.at` does reach the UI. My statement that it "never surfaces the actual wait time" was wrong.

**2. The provider's reset window is honored as a floor.** `packages/core/src/session/runner/retry.ts:43-47` returns `retryAfterMs` for `RateLimit` / `ProviderInternal`, and `Schedule.modifyDelay` (`:57-61`) uses `Duration.max(delay, minimum)`. This is pinned by a test: `packages/core/test/session-runner.test.ts:4576-4591` ("uses a larger provider retry-after delay") asserts no second request at 4999 ms and one at 5000 ms.

**3. Retries are recorded.** Every attempt publishes a durable `RetryScheduled` event carrying `attempt`, `at` and `error` (`packages/core/src/session/runner/retry.ts:62-70`), which the projector folds onto the assistant message (`packages/core/src/session/projector.ts:664`, covered by `packages/core/test/session-projector.test.ts:601`). That is the record the UI reads back.

**4. A quota-classified failure is not retried at all.** `isRetryable` returns false for `QuotaExceeded` (`retry.ts:17-38`); classification is in `packages/ai/src/provider-error.ts:61,115` (codes `insufficient_quota` / `usage_not_included` / `billing_error`, or HTTP 429 + quota text), and both are pinned by `packages/core/test/session-error.test.ts:112-130` and `packages/ai/test/provider-error.test.ts:89-100`. So for a response classified as quota exhaustion there is no retry loop to fix.

**What is left (and it is a question, not a patch).** If the Go/Zen free-tier response arrives as a plain 429 with no quota code, it is classified as `RateLimit` (`provider-error.ts:122-128`) and a short exponential backoff with a 2-3 s countdown is the expected behavior, which matches the shape you described. Two things would settle it:

1. which build you are on (the 1.x line or 2.0.x), and
2. the HTTP status plus error `code` of the response at the moment the loop starts.

If it comes back as a quota-classified error and you still see the loop, that is a real bug and I will pick it up. If it is a plain rate limit, then the fix is a policy call for the maintainers (surface the provider's real reset window when it is supplied, or treat repeated free-tier 429s as quota) rather than a missing client behavior.

One more note: your later comments about reasoning being emitted as plain text and repeated thought loops are a separate family (e.g. #49017, #48599, #49013) that maintainers are already handling, so I would keep this issue focused on the retry contract.
